newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to April 11.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to April 11.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 42.5 percent decline in its turnover during the week ending April 11, as some commercial borrowers continued to seek funds directly from banks.
Total turnover fell to 28.476 million dinars in 200 transactions, from 49.54 million dinars in 206 deals a week ago.
Traders said companies were retracted to banks for commercial borrowing as those offered slightly lower interest rates than the rest of the financial market.
They also said liquidity of the banking sector has improved after some banks managed to collect money from their debtors.

"Banks definitely have more dinars. Besides their borrowing via treasury bills has been declining for some time. And now they offer more convenient credits to companies with slightly lower interest rates," a trader told Reuters.
Traders said bank credits were available at a monthly 10-11 percent while commercial borrowing via Belgrade bourse could not be concluded below 11-12 percent per month.
For the week ending April 11, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 181 times for a volume of 24.522 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for five transactions worth 0.954 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 520 percent, while maturity stood between 10 and 30 days.
* There was one deal in the central bank short-term bonds worth three million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills rose to 31.218 million dinars from 30.884 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money rose to 17.129 million dinars from 14.95 million a week ago. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
